correctness.rationale: The projection to G distinguishes group coordinates and (0,g) is a common lower bound in every fiber, so the minimum group classes have maxima (1,g). Restrictions to idempotents and units give invariant θ and normal N; conjugating idempotents by congruent units makes N act trivially on E_X/θ. For a related pair, the maximum map first relates its units; cancelling those units recovers the idempotent relation. Conversely the map to (E_X/θ)⋊(G/N) is well-defined, multiplicative, onto and preserves the maxima. Identifying distinct atoms forces both to bottom; identifying top with an atom forces every other atom to bottom, and if top reaches bottom the relation is universal. This gives precisely the invariant bottom-block, fixed-top-atom and universal cases, with the stated kernels. Inclusion of congruences is coordinatewise. In the faithful transitive case the uncollapsed layer gives only identity, and the collapsed and universal layers each give all normal subgroups. The quotient descriptions and cyclic, alternating and symmetric group counts follow.
residual_risks: Finite checks corroborate only the examples. Ordinary congruences need not preserve the maximum map and are not classified.
